title: Flood Refund Review Horizon Where the Summit Loan Has a Resolution Deadline or Payoff Statement
content:
In settling the kept amount of a returned flood premium on a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve under Set-Aside Accounts, the horizon of the flood refund review follows the Summit loan's case records:

- **Resolution deadline.** Where the reserve's Summit loan has a maturity case (Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases) that is due and payable, or in its extension period, and that case carries a resolution deadline, the horizon of the flood refund review is the whole months from the handling date to that resolution deadline, never below zero.
- **Good-through date.** Where it has no such maturity case and a payoff case (Payoff and Loan Satisfaction) on the loan has terms issued or accepted and carries a statement good-through date, the horizon is the whole months from the handling date to that good-through date, never below zero.
- **Neither.** This rule does not set the horizon.

The maturity case decides first; a payoff case decides only when no qualifying maturity case exists. Whole months are complete calendar months from the handling date.

Hypothetical: handling date 5 November; a due-and-payable maturity case with a resolution deadline of 4 February gives 2 whole months; with the deadline on 5 February, 3.
